basic_info: 44-year-old female presenting with hematuria and pain; renal ultrasound performed for kidney stones.
present_illness: Hematuria (gross, intermittent, bright red, like cherry Kool-Aid, for six weeks) and pain (lower back, 8 out of 10, constant, associated with passing stones, resolved). Frequent urination and urgency, especially before passing stones last week. No fever, chills, or flank tenderness after the pain from passing the stones. The pain was mostly in the lower back, but now the patient feels much better. No tenderness on palpation of the back or sides. No dysuria or history of urinary tract infections reported. Patient experienced urgency and frequent urination, especially before passing stones. No changes in the urinary stream, such as difficulty starting urination, weak flow, or intermittent flow.
past_history: No relevant past history reported. Add: No history of similar episodes or previous kidney stones. Family history of kidney stones or urological conditions: Unknown (patient states they have not been asked about this before).
aux_exam: Renal ultrasound: Right kidney 10 cm long and 5 cm wide, no stones, masses, or hydronephrosis; left kidney 10.8 cm long, 6 mm stone present without obstruction. Urinalysis: Trace blood, no other abnormalities. Add: Dietary habits include high consumption of Mountain Dew, processed foods, and meat, with low intake of fruits and vegetables. Fluid intake is inadequate, with a preference for sugary drinks over water. No prior CT urography or other imaging studies reported. Patient states they have not been asked about family history of kidney stones or urological conditions, and this remains unknown.
